# clio batch

apply a list of operations in one transaction

## Usage

```
clio batch --file ops.json [--dry-run] [--bank BANK] [--actor ACTOR] [--output json|text]
clio batch --file - (reads operations JSON from stdin)
```

## Options

| Option | Kind | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--file ops.json` | text |  | Names the operations JSON file that `cli_write_batch::batch_call` decodes and hands to the `batch` tool; `-` reads the document from stdin. |
| `--dry-run` |  |  | Reports the batch plan without writing; `cli_write_batch::batch_call` sets the `batch` tool's `dry_run` argument. |
| `--bank BANK` | text |  | Scopes the batch to one bank; `cli_read_args::base_args` passes it to the `batch` tool, not to individual operations. |
| `--actor ACTOR` | text |  | Names the acting identity; `cli_read_args::base_args` passes it to the `batch` tool. |
| `--output json\|text` | enum: json, text |  | Selects the output mode that `cli_output::resolve_output` returns; the terminal decides it when absent. |

## Global options

| Option | Kind | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--db PATH` | text |  | Overrides the store address that `db_target::resolve_target` opens; config and environment decide it when absent. |
| `--backend sqlite\|postgres` | enum: sqlite, postgres |  | Selects the store backend that `db_target::resolve_target` hands to the resolver; config or the address decides it when absent. |
| `--no-input` |  |  | Refuses interactive input; `backup_restore_cli` treats a run with it as non-interactive. |
| `--yes` |  |  | Answers yes to the destructive-confirmation gate that `cli_confirm::confirmed` applies. |

## Examples

```
clio batch --file ops.json --db ./memory.db
```

preview
```
clio batch --file ops.json --dry-run -o json
```
